consequences.explanation: The accepted constraint owns readiness, exclusion, backup, publication, and recovery requirements independently of implementation status.
Readiness reports inactive, upgrade-required, recovery-required, busy, or unavailable without converting those states into false success.

The migration authoring and outgoing-revision check are the requested release safety mechanism; this decision does not authorize a new general registry, workflow store, or unrelated repository-wide guard.

payload.decision: Give every public operation a bounded metadata readiness inspection before strict model or database loading. Missing activation remains inactive and inspection does not create `.projector`, initialize SQLite or the model, or execute validators. Initialization uses an explicit bootstrap route that stages owned outputs and publishes configuration last. Active ordinary operations hold shared operation access for their whole lifetime; migration holds exclusive access, resolves unfinished governed transactions first, and retains existing writer-lease and journal behavior without nested acquisition. Add `projectorVersion` as the package release that successfully prepared the project, separate from config API, canonical schema, runtime evidence and representation versions, and SQLite schema. Accept only a validated legacy-unversioned baseline and ordered checksummed numeric-SemVer migration chains. Support upgrades across multiple releases only by traversing the full ordered verified chain; reject missing or invalid chain links, unknown or mixed versions, newer formats, tampering, and unsupported transitions without stamping current. Before mutation, create and verify a full safe `.projector` backup beneath the user's Codex data directory, including durable journals and receipts and consistent SQLite/WAL handling. Migrate in staging, validate source and target, publish with a durable pending marker, and update config last. Recovery recognizes exact migration bytes, preserves unexpected edits and backups, and returns the recovery location. Establish the permanent released format baseline only from Projector's verified TOML-converted files. Maintain one explicit net-change draft, seal immutable migrations and transform dependencies into the packaged plugin, and block outgoing revisions or release artifacts when persisted owner changes are unexplained. Ordinary edits to canonical content are not format migrations. Cooperative locks do not prove that legacy code is quiescent; the first conversion requires a supported restart disposition and held-old-runner corruption-negative evidence.
payload.title: Prepare project data before every public operation
